prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour Party Manifesto 2024 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core pitch
- “Time for change”: end Conservative “chaos,” restore stability and service-driven politics, and begin “national renewal” focused on working people.
- Mission‑driven government with clear, measurable long‑term goals and cross‑sector partnerships.

Foundations
- National security: ironclad NATO commitment; retain nuclear deterrent; Strategic Defence Review in year one; path to 2.5% of GDP on defence; strengthen counter‑terror and counter‑state threat powers.
- Secure borders: scrap Rwanda scheme; create a Border Security Command with counter‑terror style powers; hire caseworkers to clear the backlog; end hotel use; faster returns; seek EU security agreement.
- Economic stability: fiscal rules (current budget to balance; debt falling by year 5); respect OBR; recover Covid fraud; modernise HMRC; keep taxes on working people low (no rises in NI, Income Tax rates or VAT). Close avoidance: abolish non‑dom, end offshore IHT loopholes, close carried interest.

Five national missions
1) Kickstart economic growth (highest sustained in G7)
   - Pro‑business, pro‑worker “securonomics”; Industrial Strategy with a statutory council.
   - National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to crowd in private capital: ports, gigafactories, steel, CCUS, green hydrogen.
   - Cap corporation tax at 25% for the parliament; retain full expensing; replace business rates in England.
   - Planning reform for infrastructure and 1.5m homes; brownfield‑first; strategic “new towns”; more affordable/social housing; first‑time buyer support; leasehold reform.
   - Devolution: Local Growth Plans; wider mayoral powers.
   - New Deal for Working People: ban exploitative zero‑hours, end fire‑and‑rehire, day‑one rights, single enforcement body, real living wage remit.
   - Transport: rail brought into public ownership as contracts end; bus franchising/municipal ownership; EV charging push; fix 1m potholes/yr; gigabit and 5G by 2030.

2) Clean energy superpower (zero‑carbon electricity by 2030)
   - Double onshore wind, triple solar, quadruple offshore wind; invest in CCUS, hydrogen, marine; grid upgrade.
   - Nuclear: extend existing, deliver Hinkley/Sizewell C, support SMRs.
   - No new North Sea exploration licences (manage existing fields); ban fracking/coal; tougher windfall tax.
   - Great British Energy (publicly owned, £8.3bn) to co‑invest and scale local power; 650,000 jobs.
   - Warm Homes Plan: +£6.6bn to upgrade 5m homes; standards for private rentals.
   - Clean water crackdown; nature recovery; support British farming; stronger animal welfare.

3) Take back our streets
   - Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee; Respect Orders for antisocial behaviour; specific offence for assaults on shopworkers.
   - Knife crime plan: mandatory interventions; ban zombie/machete blades; accountability for online sales; Young Futures hubs nationwide.
   - Halve violence against women and girls: specialist rape units and courts; stronger stalking/spiking laws; police vetting and misconduct reform; expanded fraud strategy.
   - Prisons: build capacity; reduce reoffending via work, housing, probation reform.

4) Break down barriers to opportunity
   - 6,500 new teachers; free breakfast clubs in every primary; 3,000 school‑based nurseries.
   - Curriculum/assessment review; SEND inclusion; mental health support in every school.
   - Skills England; Technical Excellence Colleges; replace Apprenticeship Levy with flexible Growth & Skills Levy; HE funding reform; creative industries growth; football regulator.
   - Family security: UC review; renters’ rights incl. abolish Section 21; end leasehold; homelessness strategy; pensions triple lock; child poverty strategy.

5) Build an NHS fit for the future
   - 40,000 extra weekly appointments; shared waiting lists; use independent capacity; implement NHS workforce plan.
   - Double CT/MRI scanners; deliver New Hospitals Programme; NHS app upgrade; maternity safety focus.
   - Primary/community care shift: more GPs, continuity of care, pharmacist prescribing, neighbourhood health centres.
   - Dentistry Rescue Plan: 700k urgent appointments; contract reform; supervised tooth‑brushing.
   - National Care Service with national standards and a Fair Pay Agreement; 8,500 extra mental health staff.
   - Public health: smoke‑free generation; curb youth‑targeted vapes; junk food ad/energy drink measures; online safety; gambling harm reform; tackle inequalities and women’s health.

Clean politics and the Union
- Ethics and Integrity Commission; empower standards watchdog; limit MPs’ second jobs (ban paid advisory roles); Commons modernisation.
- Lords reform now (end hereditary peers; retirement at 80) and consult on replacement second chamber.
- Votes at 16; strengthen devolution; Council of the Nations and Regions.

Foreign policy and trade
- Reconnect globally; stronger UK‑EU relationship (no SM/CU/FoM), reduce trade frictions (veterinary deal, MRAs), security pact.
- Unwavering support for Ukraine; AUKUS; China strategy; defence industrial strategy; veterans’ support and visa reform.
- Targeted trade deals; Clean Power Alliance; rebuild development expertise; restore 0.7% when fiscal space allows.
